title: USB HID report descriptor: two OUTPUT fields share one usages array, and the error path frees it twice into the file scope's block allocator
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8's parse_report_descriptor (packet-usb-hid.c:3734) starts a fresh usages array after the OUTPUT append (:3790, 'field.usages = wmem_array_new(scope, sizeof(uint32_t));'), the fix's line; c702b44a01^ appends at :3347 and starts none (:3341-3350). A fix reversal, as cases 16 and 17 are. The pre-fix shape is quoted from c702b44a01^ in PROVENANCE.md.
object: an OUTPUT field's usages array header, a wmem_array_t in the file scope
lifetime_ender: the error path's wmem_free of each field's usages (:3464-3470): the shared array's chunk is freed once, then again -- a double free into the file scope's BLOCK allocator, whose recycler list lives in the freed chunks
shape: double free into the block allocator's free list
allocator_layer: block -- wmem_file_scope() (parse_report_descriptor, :3301); the free list is the recycler written over freed chunks
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator: each wmem_array_new is reduced to its two allocations (the header, sized as wmem_array_t's members, and a one-element buffer); the descriptor is INPUT, OUTPUT, OUTPUT, then a malformed item, in that order. The defective access is the second wmem_free itself.
distinguishing: the corpus's first double free, and its first row whose defective access is a call INTO the allocator: a protected arm must stop at the allocator's handback (wm_widen_probe / wm_widen), not at wm_defect_probe. Natively the double free does not alias two allocations: re-adding a chunk already on BLOCK's circular recycler relinks it to itself, and the INPUT field's freed array drops off the list -- never reissued, where the fixed sequence reissues it at once. That lost chunk is what the native fix differential's DEFECT-REPRODUCED means here; the driver's generic wording ('reached storage outside its object') does not describe it.
fault_sites_why: Declared from source before any protected run (2026-10-11). PoisonCap: the build has the port's hooks without the chunk port, so wmem_block_free begins 'ptr = wm_widen(ptr)' (wireshark-4.6.8-0002 patch, the #else of WMEM_PORT_CHUNKS), and wm_widen (src/cheribsd/poisoncap.c:172-178) loads through the pointer first; the first free poisoned and swept the chunk (wm_release_chunk, :193-198), so the second free's handed-back capability faults there. Capstone (domain and virtual) names the same handback by its label, wm_widen_probe -- declared here too, matched to that label's own instruction, never to the static function around it (src/shared/backing.c, probe() under WM_CAPABILITY), which the chunk port's wm_chunk_of calls before anything else.
status: MEASURED 2026-10-11 on every arm (R9, pre-registered 206cc3c26384, 11 of 11 as predicted): caught by the chunk port (Capstone, mode 1, at the allocator's handback probe) and by PoisonCap mode 1 (in wm_widen); missed by ASan, stock CheriBSD, the region-granular port, Sublet as the system allocator and virtual mallocng; the virtual nested arm catches it at wm_widen_probe. Native fix differential two-sided.
nested_why: wmem's BLOCK allocator carved the array header out of a block it took from g_malloc, so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NESTED.
